standard.title: Personal response and subsequent analysis
standard.description: present a personal response to a literary text comparing initial impressions and subsequent analysis of the whole text
standard.prior_knowledge: Students form and justify opinions about texts, identifying agreement and difference with others (AC9E7LE02). They have not yet compared their initial impressions with a developed whole-text analysis — the dialectic between first response and considered interpretation.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students present a personal response to a literary text that compares initial impressions with subsequent analysis of the whole text.

nodes.label: Initial response as legitimate reading
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can articulate an initial response to a literary text and recognise that first impressions are a valid starting point for analysis.
nodes.minimum_width: Record an initial response to a literary text — including emotional reactions, questions and confusion — and explain what in the text prompted each response.
nodes.typical_width: Articulate initial impressions of a literary text including what the student found compelling, confusing or significant, connecting each response to specific textual features.
wider: Compare how different students' initial responses to the same text vary, and begin to hypothesise what textual features produce those different responses
Examine how initial responses might be shaped by the reader's cultural background or prior experiences

response_modes.reason: Students often have undifferentiated initial responses ('I liked/didn't like it'). Experiencing varied texts and being asked to record specific reactions — what surprised, confused or interested them — builds the repertoire of response types that makes comparison with later analysis meaningful.

success_criteria: Student articulates at least one specific initial response (not just a general impression)
Student connects the response to a specific textual feature rather than leaving it as an unanchored feeling
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot articulate an initial response have nothing to compare against when asked to present the journey from first impression to analysis at N3 — the comparison is definitionally blocked.

nodes.label: Whole-text analysis
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop an analysis of a complete text that interrogates and makes judgements about its ideas and interpretations.
nodes.minimum_width: Develop an interpretation of a complete text that goes beyond initial impressions, using textual evidence to support a judgement about the text's ideas.
nodes.typical_width: Interrogate and make judgements about a text as a whole — comparing their own interpretation with others' ideas and reaching an independent or considered position about the text's meanings and value.
wider: Examine how reading a text a second time, with knowledge of the ending, changes the interpretation of earlier sections
Compare your interpretation of a text's central ideas against a published review or critical reading, explaining where you agree, where you diverge, and why

response_modes.reason: Moving from response to analysis requires a specific reasoning structure: from personal reaction to textual evidence to interpretation to judgement. Students need explicit scaffolding for this chain, particularly the move from 'I felt X' to 'this is produced by Y device and means Z'.

success_criteria: Student develops an interpretation that uses textual evidence to support a judgement
Student's analysis demonstrates engagement with the whole text, not just the parts that produced their initial response

nodes.label: Comparing initial and developed response
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can present a personal response that explicitly compares their initial impressions with their subsequent whole-text analysis, explaining what changed and why.
nodes.minimum_width: Present a response that identifies at least one way their initial impression changed after whole-text analysis, and explains what the analysis revealed that the initial impression missed.
nodes.typical_width: Present a personal response to a literary text that traces the journey from initial impressions to developed interpretation — explaining what the analysis added, complicated or confirmed, and arriving at an independent position.
wider: Examine how the process of sharing initial responses with others before detailed analysis affects subsequent interpretation — and what this reveals about reading as a social process
Reflect on a text where initial and final response are significantly different, and analyse what this reveals about the text's complexity or the reader's assumptions

response_modes.reason: Presenting a response that integrates initial impression and subsequent analysis — showing how one led to or was transformed by the other — requires students to hold both simultaneously and articulate the relationship. This is the core capability of the descriptor.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The metacognitive dimension — how reading changes the reader — is genuinely enriching territory for Y9. Advancing students can explore how texts resist, challenge or confirm readers' expectations, which is a sophisticated literary insight that stays within Y9 scope.
success_criteria: Student explicitly compares an initial impression with their subsequent analysis
Student explains what the fuller analysis revealed that the initial impression could not have accessed
